15: # Claude Code Agent Delegation Reference
16: 
17: Reach for this when a task needs a named Claude Code agent instead of a bare `claude -p` prompt, and pick the flags that keep that hand-off read-only or scoped.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: ### Purpose
24: 
25: Documents the active Claude Code agents in `.claude/agents/` and how external AI assistants orchestrate them. The calling AI (OpenCode, Copilot, etc.) acts as the **conductor** (planner, validator, integrator) while Claude Code executes targeted tasks through its agent system.
26: 
27: ### When to Use
28: 
29: - Delegating supplementary implementation or analysis tasks to Claude Code agents
30: - Cross-AI code review or architectural second opinion via `@review`
31: - Deep reasoning and extended thinking via `@ai-council`
32: - Fresh-perspective debugging after the calling AI's attempts fail via Task-tool dispatch to `@debug`
33: - Codebase exploration in read-only mode via `@context`
34: 
35: ### Core Principle
36: 
37: The calling AI decides WHAT to do, Claude Code decides HOW to do it within the delegated scope.
38: 
39: ---
40: 
41: ## 2. ORCHESTRATION MODEL
42: 
43: ```
44: External AI (CONDUCTOR)               [OpenCode / Copilot / etc.]
45:   |
46:   |-- Analyzes task, selects Claude Code agent
47:   |-- Constructs claude CLI command with --agent flag
48:   |-- Delegates via Bash/shell execution
49:   |
50:   v
51: Claude Code CLI (EXECUTOR)
52:   |
53:   |-- Loads agent definition from .skilled/agents/<name>.md
54:   |-- Loads CLAUDE.md context hierarchy (global → project → local)
55:   |-- Executes with agent-specific instructions and tool permissions
56:   |-- Returns output to stdout
57:   |
58:   v
59: External AI (CONDUCTOR)
60:   |
61:   |-- Validates output quality and relevance
62:   |-- Integrates findings into its own workflow
63:   |-- Decides next step (accept, iterate, delegate elsewhere)
64: ```
65: 
66: ### Invocation Pattern
67: 
68: Claude Code agents are routed using the `--agent` flag with an agent name. Agent definitions live in `.claude/agents/<name>.md` files. For read-only tasks, combine with `--permission-mode plan`.
69: 
70: ```bash
71: # Agent-based delegation (non-interactive)
72: claude -p "Review src/auth.ts for security issues" \
73:   --agent review --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
74: 
75: # Agent with specific model
76: claude -p "Plan the authentication redesign with multi-strategy analysis" \
77:   --agent ai-council --model claude-opus-5-5 --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
78: 
79: # Agent with file context
80: claude -p "Debug this error in @src/auth/handler.ts: [paste error]" \
81:   --agent debug --output-format text 2>&1
82: 
83: # Capture output to file
84: claude -p "Map the dependency graph for src/" \
85:   --agent context --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1 > /tmp/context-map.txt
86: 
87: # Agent with cost control (no dedicated speckit agent -- markdown handles spec-doc authoring)
88: claude -p "Generate spec documentation for the new feature" \
89:   --agent markdown --max-budget-usd 0.50 --output-format text 2>&1
90: ```
91: 
92: ### Agent Definition Structure
93: 
94: Each agent is defined in a `.md` file in `.claude/agents/` (the Claude Code runtime directory — NOT `.opencode/agents/`, which is the OpenCode runtime's own directory; both are kept in sync by the repo's agent-mirror-sync CI check, but Claude Code itself resolves from `.claude/agents/`):
95: 
96: ```
97: .claude/agents/
98: ├── ai-council.md       # Multi-strategy planning (scoped-write: ai-council/** only)
99: ├── code.md             # Application-code implementation via sk-code
100: ├── context.md          # Read-only codebase exploration
101: ├── debug.md            # Systematic debugging
102: ├── deep-research.md    # Single-iteration deep research (command-owned)
103: ├── deep-review.md      # Single-iteration deep review (command-owned)
104: ├── design.md           # Decides UI values via sk-design; measures a surface via sk-design-md-generator
105: ├── markdown.md         # Template-first markdown/documentation execution
106: ├── orchestrate.md      # Multi-agent coordination
107: ├── prompt-improver.md  # Dispatch-ready prompt packages (command-owned)
108: └── review.md           # Code review, security audits
109: ```
110: 
111: There is no `handover.md`, `research.md`, `speckit.md`, or `write.md` in the current roster.
112: 
113: ---
114: 
115: ## 3. CLAUDE CODE AGENT CATALOG
116: 
117: ### Agent Roster (11 Agents)
118: 
119: | Agent | Permission Mode | Purpose | Use When |
120: |-------|-----------------|---------|----------|
121: | `context` | `plan` (read-only) | Read-only codebase exploration, file discovery, pattern analysis | You need to understand code structure, dependencies, or patterns before implementing |
122: | `debug` | default | Systematic debugging, root cause analysis, fresh perspective | Calling AI's debugging attempts failed; need independent root cause analysis |
123: | `orchestrate` | `plan` (read-only) | Multi-agent coordination, complex workflow decomposition | Running multiple Claude Code agents for interconnected tasks |
124: | `deep-research` | default | Evidence gathering, feasibility analysis, comparative technical investigation | Need current best practices, technical comparisons, or feasibility assessment. Command-owned by `/deep:research` for iterative loops; a single ad-hoc dispatch is fine for a one-shot comparison |
125: | `review` | `plan` (read-only) | Code review, security audits, quality scoring, architecture review | Second opinion on generated code, architecture, or security posture |
126: | `ai-council` | `plan` (planning) + scoped-write to `ai-council/**` | Multi-strategy planning, diverse reasoning strategies, scored rubric | Complex planning requiring multiple perspectives scored by quality dimensions |
127: | `markdown` | default | Template-first documentation generation, README creation, guide writing, spec-folder scaffolding | Creating or updating technical documentation, guides, READMEs, or spec docs |
128: | `code` | default | Application-code implementation via `sk-code` | Implementing an approved plan; orchestrator-only dispatch |
129: | `design` | default | Decides UI values via `sk-design`; measures a surface via `sk-design-md-generator` | Choosing spacing, type, color, shadow or motion values; diagnosing a UI complaint; reviewing UI for accessibility; or extracting a measured Style Reference from a live source UI |
130: | `deep-review` | default | Single-iteration severity-tagged code review | Command-owned by `/deep:review` — never dispatch directly for the iterative loop |
131: | `prompt-improver` | default | Dispatch-ready prompt package generation | Command-owned by `/prompt`'s deep-path escalation — never dispatch directly |
132: 
133: ---
134: 
135: ## 4. AGENT DETAILS
136: 
137: ### @context — Codebase Explorer
138: 
139: **Purpose:** Read-only codebase exploration, file discovery, dependency mapping, pattern analysis.
140: 
141: **Best for:** Understanding unfamiliar code before implementing, mapping cross-file dependencies, creating architecture overviews.
142: 
143: **Recommended flags:** `--permission-mode plan` (enforces read-only)
144: 
145: ```bash
146: # Map project architecture
147: claude -p "Analyze the architecture of this project. Identify key modules, entry points, and dependency flow." \
148:   --agent context --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
149: 
150: # Find patterns
151: claude -p "Find all authentication-related files and describe the auth flow" \
152:   --agent context --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
153: 
154: # Dependency analysis
155: claude -p "Map the import graph for @src/services/ — what depends on what?" \
156:   --agent context --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
157: ```
158: 
159: ---
160: 
161: ### @debug — Systematic Debugger
162: 
163: **Purpose:** Root cause analysis, systematic debugging with fresh perspective, error reproduction strategies.
164: 
165: **Best for:** When the calling AI's debugging attempts have failed and a fresh perspective is needed.
166: 
167: **Recommended flags:** default permission mode (may need to read and write debug artifacts)
168: 
169: ```bash
170: # Fresh-perspective debugging
171: claude -p "Debug this error. My analysis so far: [paste context]. Error: [paste error]" \
172:   --agent debug --output-format text 2>&1
173: 
174: # Root cause analysis
175: claude -p "Users report intermittent 500 errors on /api/orders. Analyze @src/api/orders.ts and @src/services/order.ts for potential race conditions or unhandled errors." \
176:   --agent debug --output-format text 2>&1
177: 
178: # Error reproduction
179: claude -p "This test fails intermittently: [test name]. Analyze @[test file] and suggest reproduction steps." \
180:   --agent debug --output-format text 2>&1
181: ```
182: 
183: ---
184: 
185: ### @orchestrate — Multi-Agent Coordinator
186: 
187: **Purpose:** Coordinate multiple Claude Code agents, decompose complex workflows, manage agent pipelines.
188: 
189: **Best for:** Complex tasks that benefit from multiple agent perspectives in sequence.
190: 
191: **Recommended flags:** `--permission-mode plan` (coordination is read-only planning)
192: 
193: ```bash
194: # Coordinate review and testing
195: claude -p "Coordinate a comprehensive review of the payment module: first explore architecture, then review code, then identify test gaps." \
196:   --agent orchestrate --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
197: ```
198: 
199: ---
200: 
201: ### @deep-research — Evidence Gatherer
202: 
203: **Purpose:** Iterative technical investigation, feasibility analysis, best practices research, comparative analysis.
204: 
205: **Best for:** Gathering evidence for architectural decisions, comparing technologies, assessing feasibility.
206: 
207: ```bash
208: # Technology comparison
209: claude -p "Compare Redis vs Memcached for our session storage needs. Consider: performance, clustering, persistence, data structures." \
210:   --agent deep-research --output-format text 2>&1
211: 
212: # Feasibility analysis
213: claude -p "Assess the feasibility of migrating from REST to GraphQL for @src/api/. Consider codebase size, team impact, and migration path." \
214:   --agent deep-research --output-format text 2>&1
215: ```
216: 
217: ---
218: 
219: ### @review — Code Reviewer
220: 
221: **Purpose:** Code review, security audits, architecture review, quality scoring.
222: 
223: **Best for:** Second-opinion code review, security vulnerability detection, architecture quality assessment.
224: 
225: **Recommended flags:** `--permission-mode plan` (review should be read-only)
226: 
227: ```bash
228: # Security review
229: claude -p "Review @src/auth/ for security vulnerabilities. Check for: XSS, CSRF, injection, auth bypass, insecure defaults." \
230:   --agent review --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
231: 
232: # Architecture review
233: claude -p "Review the overall architecture of src/services/. Assess: coupling, cohesion, separation of concerns, error handling patterns." \
234:   --agent review --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
235: 
236: # Quality scoring
237: claude -p "Score the code quality of @src/utils.ts on: readability (1-10), maintainability (1-10), test coverage potential (1-10), security (1-10)." \
238:   --agent review --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
239: ```
240: 
241: ---
242: 
243: ### @ai-council — Multi-Strategy Planner
244: 
245: **Purpose:** Multi-strategy planning with diverse reasoning approaches, scored by quality dimensions.
246: 
247: **Best for:** Complex planning tasks that benefit from multiple reasoning strategies evaluated by rubric.
248: 
249: **Recommended flags:** `--permission-mode plan` (planning is read-only), `--model claude-opus-5-5` (deep reasoning)
250: 
251: ```bash
252: # Multi-strategy architecture planning
253: claude -p "Plan the authentication system redesign. Consider: session-based vs JWT vs OAuth2. Evaluate each strategy across security, scalability, complexity, and team expertise." \
254:   --agent ai-council --model claude-opus-5-5 --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
255: 
256: # Complex migration planning
257: claude -p "Plan the database migration from MongoDB to PostgreSQL. Evaluate strategies: big-bang, gradual, dual-write. Score each on risk, downtime, complexity, rollback ability." \
258:   --agent ai-council --model claude-opus-5-5 --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
259: ```
260: 
261: ---
262: 
263: ## 5. QUICK REFERENCE
264: 
265: ### Quick Selection
266: 
267: ```
268: What is the primary need?
269: 
270: UNDERSTAND CODE       → @context (with --permission-mode plan)
271: FIX A BUG            → @debug
272: REVIEW CODE          → @review (with --permission-mode plan)
273: PLAN ARCHITECTURE    → @ai-council (with --model claude-opus-5-5)
274: RESEARCH A TOPIC     → @deep-research
275: COORDINATE AGENTS    → @orchestrate (with --permission-mode plan)
276: SPEC PACKET WORK     → Main agent + `/speckit:plan --intake-only` or `/speckit:plan`
277: SAVE CONTINUITY      → `/speckit:save`
278: ```
279: 
280: ### Model + Agent Combinations
281: 
282: | Scenario | Agent | Model | Flags |
283: |----------|-------|-------|-------|
284: | Quick code review | `review` | sonnet (default) | `--permission-mode plan` |
285: | Deep security audit | `review` | `claude-opus-5-5` | `--permission-mode plan --effort high` |
286: | Architecture planning | `ai-council` | `claude-opus-5-5` | `--permission-mode plan --effort high` |
287: | Fast codebase scan | `context` | `claude-haiku-5-5` | `--permission-mode plan` |
288: | Research + write | `deep-research` | sonnet (default) | (default) |
289: | Emergency debugging | `debug` | `claude-opus-5-5` | `--effort high` |
290: 
291: ---
292: 
293: ## 6. BEST PRACTICES
294: 
295: ### Do
296: 
297: - **Match agent to task** — Use the routing guide above instead of generic prompts
298: - **Use `--permission-mode plan`** for all read-only agents (context, review, orchestrate, ai-council)
299: - **Include file references** with `@` for targeted analysis instead of broad prompts
300: - **Capture output** to files for multi-step workflows: `> /tmp/output.txt`
301: - **Use Opus for deep reasoning** but Sonnet for standard tasks to manage costs
302: - **Validate all output** before integrating into the calling AI's workflow
303: 
304: ### Don't
305: 
306: - **Don't delegate trivial tasks** — CLI overhead isn't worth it for simple questions
307: - **Don't skip validation** — Claude Code output needs review like any AI output
308: - **Don't use `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`** without explicit user approval
309: - **Don't nest Claude Code** — check `$CLAUDECODE` env var before invoking
310: - **Don't forget `2>&1`** — always capture stderr for error handling
311: - **Don't ignore costs** — use `--max-budget-usd` for batch operations

75: # Agent with specific model
76: claude -p "Plan the authentication redesign with multi-strategy analysis" \
77:   --agent ai-council --model claude-opus-5-5 --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
78: 
79: # Agent with file context
80: claude -p "Debug this error in @src/auth/handler.ts: [paste error]" \
81:   --agent debug --output-format text 2>&1
82: 
83: # Capture output to file
84: claude -p "Map the dependency graph for src/" \
85:   --agent context --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1 > /tmp/context-map.txt
86: 
87: # Agent with cost control (no dedicated speckit agent -- markdown handles spec-doc authoring)
88: claude -p "Generate spec documentation for the new feature" \
89:   --agent markdown --max-budget-usd 0.50 --output-format text 2>&1
90: ```
91: 
92: ### Agent Definition Structure
93: 
94: Each agent is defined in a `.md` file in `.claude/agents/` (the Claude Code runtime directory — NOT `.opencode/agents/`, which is the OpenCode runtime's own directory; both are kept in sync by the repo's agent-mirror-sync CI check, but Claude Code itself resolves from `.claude/agents/`):
95: 
96: ```
97: .claude/agents/
98: ├── ai-council.md       # Multi-strategy planning (scoped-write: ai-council/** only)
99: ├── code.md             # Application-code implementation via sk-code
100: ├── context.md          # Read-only codebase exploration
101: ├── debug.md            # Systematic debugging
102: ├── deep-research.md    # Single-iteration deep research (command-owned)
103: ├── deep-review.md      # Single-iteration deep review (command-owned)
104: ├── design.md           # Decides UI values via sk-design; measures a surface via sk-design-md-generator
105: ├── markdown.md         # Template-first markdown/documentation execution
106: ├── orchestrate.md      # Multi-agent coordination
107: ├── prompt-improver.md  # Dispatch-ready prompt packages (command-owned)
108: └── review.md           # Code review, security audits
109: ```
110: 
111: There is no `handover.md`, `research.md`, `speckit.md`, or `write.md` in the current roster.
112: 
113: ---
114: 
115: ## 3. CLAUDE CODE AGENT CATALOG
116: 
117: ### Agent Roster (11 Agents)
118: 
119: | Agent | Permission Mode | Purpose | Use When |
120: |-------|-----------------|---------|----------|
121: | `context` | `plan` (read-only) | Read-only codebase exploration, file discovery, pattern analysis | You need to understand code structure, dependencies, or patterns before implementing |
122: | `debug` | default | Systematic debugging, root cause analysis, fresh perspective | Calling AI's debugging attempts failed; need independent root cause analysis |
123: | `orchestrate` | `plan` (read-only) | Multi-agent coordination, complex workflow decomposition | Running multiple Claude Code agents for interconnected tasks |
124: | `deep-research` | default | Evidence gathering, feasibility analysis, comparative technical investigation | Need current best practices, technical comparisons, or feasibility assessment. Command-owned by `/deep:research` for iterative loops; a single ad-hoc dispatch is fine for a one-shot comparison |
125: | `review` | `plan` (read-only) | Code review, security audits, quality scoring, architecture review | Second opinion on generated code, architecture, or security posture |
126: | `ai-council` | `plan` (planning) + scoped-write to `ai-council/**` | Multi-strategy planning, diverse reasoning strategies, scored rubric | Complex planning requiring multiple perspectives scored by quality dimensions |
127: | `markdown` | default | Template-first documentation generation, README creation, guide writing, spec-folder scaffolding | Creating or updating technical documentation, guides, READMEs, or spec docs |
128: | `code` | default | Application-code implementation via `sk-code` | Implementing an approved plan; orchestrator-only dispatch |
129: | `design` | default | Decides UI values via `sk-design`; measures a surface via `sk-design-md-generator` | Choosing spacing, type, color, shadow or motion values; diagnosing a UI complaint; reviewing UI for accessibility; or extracting a measured Style Reference from a live source UI |
130: | `deep-review` | default | Single-iteration severity-tagged code review | Command-owned by `/deep:review` — never dispatch directly for the iterative loop |
131: | `prompt-improver` | default | Dispatch-ready prompt package generation | Command-owned by `/prompt`'s deep-path escalation — never dispatch directly |
132: 
133: ---
134: 
135: ## 4. AGENT DETAILS
136: 
137: ### @context — Codebase Explorer
138: 
139: **Purpose:** Read-only codebase exploration, file discovery, dependency mapping, pattern analysis.
140: 
141: **Best for:** Understanding unfamiliar code before implementing, mapping cross-file dependencies, creating architecture overviews.
142: 
143: **Recommended flags:** `--permission-mode plan` (enforces read-only)
144: 
145: ```bash
146: # Map project architecture
147: claude -p "Analyze the architecture of this project. Identify key modules, entry points, and dependency flow." \
148:   --agent context --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
149: 
150: # Find patterns
151: claude -p "Find all authentication-related files and describe the auth flow" \
152:   --agent context --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
153: 
154: # Dependency analysis
155: claude -p "Map the import graph for @src/services/ — what depends on what?" \
156:   --agent context --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
157: ```
158: 
159: ---
160: 
161: ### @debug — Systematic Debugger
162: 
163: **Purpose:** Root cause analysis, systematic debugging with fresh perspective, error reproduction strategies.
164: 
165: **Best for:** When the calling AI's debugging attempts have failed and a fresh perspective is needed.
166: 
167: **Recommended flags:** default permission mode (may need to read and write debug artifacts)
168: 
169: ```bash
170: # Fresh-perspective debugging
171: claude -p "Debug this error. My analysis so far: [paste context]. Error: [paste error]" \
172:   --agent debug --output-format text 2>&1
173: 
174: # Root cause analysis
175: claude -p "Users report intermittent 500 errors on /api/orders. Analyze @src/api/orders.ts and @src/services/order.ts for potential race conditions or unhandled errors." \
176:   --agent debug --output-format text 2>&1
177: 
178: # Error reproduction
179: claude -p "This test fails intermittently: [test name]. Analyze @[test file] and suggest reproduction steps." \
180:   --agent debug --output-format text 2>&1
181: ```
182: 
183: ---
184: 
185: ### @orchestrate — Multi-Agent Coordinator
186: 
187: **Purpose:** Coordinate multiple Claude Code agents, decompose complex workflows, manage agent pipelines.
188: 
189: **Best for:** Complex tasks that benefit from multiple agent perspectives in sequence.
190: 
191: **Recommended flags:** `--permission-mode plan` (coordination is read-only planning)
192: 
193: ```bash
194: # Coordinate review and testing
195: claude -p "Coordinate a comprehensive review of the payment module: first explore architecture, then review code, then identify test gaps." \
196:   --agent orchestrate --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
197: ```
198: 
199: ---
200: 
201: ### @deep-research — Evidence Gatherer
202: 
203: **Purpose:** Iterative technical investigation, feasibility analysis, best practices research, comparative analysis.
204: 
205: **Best for:** Gathering evidence for architectural decisions, comparing technologies, assessing feasibility.
206: 
207: ```bash
208: # Technology comparison
209: claude -p "Compare Redis vs Memcached for our session storage needs. Consider: performance, clustering, persistence, data structures." \
210:   --agent deep-research --output-format text 2>&1
211: 
212: # Feasibility analysis
213: claude -p "Assess the feasibility of migrating from REST to GraphQL for @src/api/. Consider codebase size, team impact, and migration path." \
214:   --agent deep-research --output-format text 2>&1
215: ```
216: 
217: ---
218: 
219: ### @review — Code Reviewer
220: 
221: **Purpose:** Code review, security audits, architecture review, quality scoring.
222: 
223: **Best for:** Second-opinion code review, security vulnerability detection, architecture quality assessment.
224: 
225: **Recommended flags:** `--permission-mode plan` (review should be read-only)
226: 
227: ```bash
228: # Security review
229: claude -p "Review @src/auth/ for security vulnerabilities. Check for: XSS, CSRF, injection, auth bypass, insecure defaults." \
230:   --agent review --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
231: 
232: # Architecture review
233: claude -p "Review the overall architecture of src/services/. Assess: coupling, cohesion, separation of concerns, error handling patterns." \
234:   --agent review --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
235: 
236: # Quality scoring
237: claude -p "Score the code quality of @src/utils.ts on: readability (1-10), maintainability (1-10), test coverage potential (1-10), security (1-10)." \
238:   --agent review --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
239: ```
240: 
241: ---
242: 
243: ### @ai-council — Multi-Strategy Planner
244: 
245: **Purpose:** Multi-strategy planning with diverse reasoning approaches, scored by quality dimensions.
246: 
247: **Best for:** Complex planning tasks that benefit from multiple reasoning strategies evaluated by rubric.
248: 
249: **Recommended flags:** `--permission-mode plan` (planning is read-only), `--model claude-opus-5-5` (deep reasoning)
250: 
251: ```bash
252: # Multi-strategy architecture planning
253: claude -p "Plan the authentication system redesign. Consider: session-based vs JWT vs OAuth2. Evaluate each strategy across security, scalability, complexity, and team expertise." \
254:   --agent ai-council --model claude-opus-5-5 --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
255: 
256: # Complex migration planning
257: claude -p "Plan the database migration from MongoDB to PostgreSQL. Evaluate strategies: big-bang, gradual, dual-write. Score each on risk, downtime, complexity, rollback ability." \
258:   --agent ai-council --model claude-opus-5-5 --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1
259: ```
260: 
261: ---
262: 
263: ## 5. QUICK REFERENCE
264: 
265: ### Quick Selection
266: 
267: ```
268: What is the primary need?
269: 
270: UNDERSTAND CODE       → @context (with --permission-mode plan)
271: FIX A BUG            → @debug
272: REVIEW CODE          → @review (with --permission-mode plan)
273: PLAN ARCHITECTURE    → @ai-council (with --model claude-opus-5-5)
274: RESEARCH A TOPIC     → @deep-research
275: COORDINATE AGENTS    → @orchestrate (with --permission-mode plan)
276: SPEC PACKET WORK     → Main agent + `/speckit:plan --intake-only` or `/speckit:plan`
277: SAVE CONTINUITY      → `/speckit:save`
278: ```
279: 
280: ### Model + Agent Combinations
281: 
282: | Scenario | Agent | Model | Flags |
283: |----------|-------|-------|-------|
284: | Quick code review | `review` | sonnet (default) | `--permission-mode plan` |
285: | Deep security audit | `review` | `claude-opus-5-5` | `--permission-mode plan --effort high` |
286: | Architecture planning | `ai-council` | `claude-opus-5-5` | `--permission-mode plan --effort high` |
287: | Fast codebase scan | `context` | `claude-haiku-5-5` | `--permission-mode plan` |
288: | Research + write | `deep-research` | sonnet (default) | (default) |
289: | Emergency debugging | `debug` | `claude-opus-5-5` | `--effort high` |
290: 
291: ---
292: 
293: ## 6. BEST PRACTICES
294: 
295: ### Do
296: 
297: - **Match agent to task** — Use the routing guide above instead of generic prompts
298: - **Use `--permission-mode plan`** for all read-only agents (context, review, orchestrate, ai-council)
299: - **Include file references** with `@` for targeted analysis instead of broad prompts
300: - **Capture output** to files for multi-step workflows: `> /tmp/output.txt`
301: - **Use Opus for deep reasoning** but Sonnet for standard tasks to manage costs
302: - **Validate all output** before integrating into the calling AI's workflow
303: 
304: ### Don't
305: 
306: - **Don't delegate trivial tasks** — CLI overhead isn't worth it for simple questions
307: - **Don't skip validation** — Claude Code output needs review like any AI output
308: - **Don't use `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`** without explicit user approval
309: - **Don't nest Claude Code** — check `$CLAUDECODE` env var before invoking
310: - **Don't forget `2>&1`** — always capture stderr for error handling
311: - **Don't ignore costs** — use `--max-budget-usd` for batch operations

44: 
45: **Deep extended-thinking reasoning.** Claude's extended thinking produces detailed internal reasoning before responding, leading to higher quality outputs for complex tasks. 17: # Claude Code CLI - Complete Command Reference
18: 
19: Open this at dispatch time, when the command has to be right the first time: the tables answer what a switch does and what a failed run means.
20: 
21: ---
22: 
23: ## 1. OVERVIEW
24: 
25: ### Purpose
26: 
27: Provide a comprehensive, single-source reference for all Claude Code CLI commands, flags, models, configuration options, permission modes, and troubleshooting guidance for external AI assistants delegating tasks.
28: 
29: ### When to Use
30: 
31: - Setting up or configuring Claude Code CLI
32: - Looking up command-line flags, subcommands, or agent configurations
33: - Troubleshooting authentication, permission, or session issues
34: - Selecting the right model and permission mode for a task
35: - Understanding output formats and structured output options
36: 
37: ### Core Principle
38: 
39: Claude Code is Anthropic's official CLI for Claude, providing terminal-based AI coding assistance powered by Claude models (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku). It offers deep reasoning via extended thinking, surgical code editing, schema-validated structured output, agent delegation, and persistent memory — all from the command line.
40: 
41: ### Key Sources
42: 
43: | Source | URL |
44: |--------|-----|
45: | **Repository** | [anthropics/claude-code](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code) |
46: | **Documentation** | [Claude Code documentation](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code) |
47: | **License** | Proprietary (Anthropic) |
48: | **Runtime** | Node.js 18+ |
49: 
50: ---
51: 
52: ## 2. INSTALLATION
53: 
54: | Method | Command | Notes |
55: |--------|---------|-------|
56: | **npm global** | `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` | Persistent install, recommended |
57: | **Upgrade** | `npm update -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` or `claude update` | Update to latest version |
58: 
59: **Platform support:**
60: 
61: | Platform | Status |
62: |----------|--------|
63: | macOS | Full support |
64: | Linux | Full support |
65: | Windows | Experimental |
66: 
67: After installation, run `claude` for interactive mode or `claude -p "prompt"` for non-interactive use.
68: 
69: ---
70: 
71: ## 3. AUTHENTICATION
72: 
73: cli-claude-code authenticates through the **Claude subscription OAuth only**. It does not use an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
74: 
75: | Method | Setup | Best For |
76: |--------|-------|----------|
77: | **OAuth** | `claude auth login` (browser flow) | Personal use, interactive |
78: | **Token Setup** | `claude setup-token` | Non-interactive CI/CD pipelines (long-lived OAuth token) |
79: 
80: **OAuth login/logout:**
81: 
82: ```bash
83: # Authenticate via browser (opens OAuth flow)
84: claude auth login
85: 
86: # View authentication status
87: claude auth status
88: 
89: # Log out
90: claude auth logout
91: ```
92: 
93: **Non-interactive token setup (CI/CD):**
94: 
95: ```bash
96: # Generate a long-lived OAuth token for headless environments
97: claude setup-token
98: ```
99: 
100: ---
101: 
102: ## 4. CORE INVOCATION
103: 
104: ### Non-Interactive Mode (Primary for Cross-AI)
105:

23: ## 1. OVERVIEW

25: ### Purpose

27: Provide a comprehensive, single-source reference for all Claude Code CLI commands, flags, models, configuration options, permission modes, and troubleshooting guidance for external AI assistants delegating tasks.

37: ### Core Principle
38: 
39: Claude Code is Anthropic's official CLI for Claude, providing terminal-based AI coding assistance powered by Claude models (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku). It offers deep reasoning via extended thinking, surgical code editing, schema-validated structured output, agent delegation, and persistent memory — all from the command line.

22: 
23: ### Purpose
24: 
25: One place to answer "which model, which effort, how to dispatch" for cli-claude-code.
26: 
27: ### When to Use
28: - Choosing a `--model claude-*` id for a `claude -p` dispatch

30: - Recalling the default model and the canonical non-interactive invocation shape
31: 
32: ### Core Principle
33: 
34: This mode is single-provider (Anthropic) and always reaches a small, fixed roster — so this file IS the catalog, with every model id inline.
35: 
36: ### Scope
37: This file enumerates the model/effort facts and the dispatch envelope. It does NOT own: the full `claude` flag surface, permission modes, auth pre-flight, and troubleshooting (see [cli-reference.md](./cli-reference.md)), per-model prompt-craft (see §6), or the fan-out / model-enforcement runtime (see §6).

39: ### Authority pointers
40: - Full CLI flags, subcommands, permission modes, OAuth pre-flight, troubleshooting → [cli-reference.md](./cli-reference.md)
41: - Dispatch shapes + orchestration patterns → [integration-patterns.md](./integration-patterns.md)
42: - Live model availability on a given install → the calling environment's `--model` support
43: 
44: ---
45: 
46: ## 2. PROVIDERS & MODELS
47: 
48: cli-claude-code is single-provider: **Anthropic**. The model string passed to `--model` is always a `claude-*` id. The roster below is complete. Pin the exact id; the CLI also accepts the aliases `opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku` and `fable`, which resolve to the newest id in each family.
49: 
50: ### Anthropic
51: 
52: | Model id | Default? | Role | Efforts |
53: |----------|----------|------|---------|
54: | `claude-sonnet-5-5` | **Default** | Sonnet 5.5, balanced: general tasks, code generation, reviews | all five |
55: | `claude-opus-5-5` | no | Opus 5.5, deepest Opus reasoning: architecture, complex trade-offs, subtle root causes | all five |
56: | `claude-haiku-5-5` | no | Haiku 5.5, fastest and cheapest: classification, formatting, simple queries, batch work. Use when the caller asks for it | all five |
57: | `claude-fable-5-1` | no | Fable 5.1, the current Fable. The CLI's model catalog names `fable` as its `best` alias | all five |
58: 
59: > **No Fable 5.5 yet.** Claude Code 2.1.293 rejects `claude-fable-5-5` with `unrecognized_model`, and its `fable` alias resolves to `claude-fable-5-1`. Pin `claude-fable-5-1`, or pass `--model fable` to get whichever Fable the installed CLI knows. Recheck with `claude -p --model claude-fable-5-5 --effort low "Reply with OK" </dev/null 2>&1` after a CLI update.
60: 
61: **Replaced ids.** The previous default `claude-sonnet-4-6` and the earlier `claude-sonnet-5` give way to `claude-sonnet-5-5`, and `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` gives way to `claude-haiku-5-5`. The old ids were not probed when this roster was refreshed, so pin one only after confirming it answers.
62: 
63: ---
64: 
65: ## 3. DEFAULTS & QUICK INVOCATION
66: 
67: Dispatch this mode's default without opening any other file:
68: 
69: | Field | Value |
70: |-------|-------|
71: | Default model | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
72: | Default effort | none passed; the child resolves it (see §4) |
73: | Default format | `--output-format text` |
74: 
75: ```bash
76: claude -p "<prompt>" \
77:   --model claude-sonnet-5-5 \
78:   --output-format text \
79:   2>&1
80: ```
81: 
82: - Always append `2>&1` to capture both stdout and stderr.
83: - For deep-reasoning work, override with `--model claude-opus-5-5 --effort high`, and raise the effort to `xhigh` or `max` when `high` is not enough.
84: - If Claude Code is not authenticated, the mode ASKS the operator to run `claude auth login`; it never substitutes an API key or a different model. See the OAuth pre-flight decision tree in [cli-reference.md](./cli-reference.md) §3 and the SKILL's "Provider Auth Pre-Flight".
85: 
86: **Why Sonnet 5.5 is the default.** It answered a live probe, it is what the `sonnet` alias resolves to, and it keeps the default in the same balanced family as before, so a caller that names no model gets the same cost and depth profile on the current generation. Opus and Fable stay opt-in for work that needs more depth.
87: 
88: ---
89: 
90: ## 4. REASONING-EFFORT / THINKING LEVER
91: 
92: cli-claude-code expresses reasoning depth through the **`--effort`** flag. Every model in §2 takes all five levels: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` and `max`. Claude Code 2.1.293 lists those five values in `claude --help`, and its model catalog marks each roster model with the `effort`, `xhigh_effort` and `max_effort` capabilities.
93: 
94: | Level | Flag | When to use it |
95: |-------|------|----------------|
96: | Low | `--effort low` | Classification, formatting, quick lookups, mechanical edits. Fastest and cheapest |
97: | Medium | `--effort medium` | Routine edits and short reviews. The built-in default of the 5.5 models |
98: | High | `--effort high` | Standard code generation, reviews and debugging. The usual pairing with Opus |
99: | Extra high | `--effort xhigh` | Architecture, hard trade-offs, subtle root causes, deep reviews |
100: | Max | `--effort max` | The hardest problems, where cost is secondary. Pair it with `--max-budget-usd` |
101: 
102: **When the flag is omitted.** The child takes the effort its loaded settings give it, a top-level `effortLevel` or a per-model entry under `modelSettings`, and otherwise the model's built-in default. Those settings set a model's default only. They never remove a level, so `--effort` always reaches all five. Pass `--effort` whenever the depth matters, so the result does not depend on the machine's settings.
103: 
104: ---
105: 
106: ## 5. HOW TO INVOKE
107: 
108: ### Self-invocation guard
109: A `claude -p` dispatch must never run from inside a Claude Code session (a `$CLAUDECODE`-set, `claude`-in-ancestry, or state-lock signal) — that is a circular self-invocation. The guard is inline in [../ROUTER.md](../ROUTER.md) §3 "Self-Invocation Guard".
110: 
111: ### Dispatch envelope (child / detached sessions)
112: When dispatching as a non-interactive child (spec-gate-neutralized worker), prefix the shared env and capture stderr:
113: 
114: ```bash
115: SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 claude -p "<prompt>" \
116:   --model claude-sonnet-5-5 --output-format text 2>&1
117: ```
118: 
119: - `SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` — neutralizes the spec-gate for a bound child worker so it does not stall on an interactive Gate-3 answer, and marks the run as an orchestrated sub-session so the worktree wrapper exec's in place rather than allocating its own worktree. See [../SKILL.md](../SKILL.md) §4 Rule 13.
120: - `2>&1` — REQUIRED to capture stderr; without it error and warning messages are lost. See [integration-patterns.md](./integration-patterns.md).
121: - `-p` (print) is mandatory for non-interactive dispatch; use `--permission-mode plan` for read-only review/analysis.
122: 
123: ### Parallel / fan-out
124: Multi-lineage parallel dispatch is driven by `fanout-run.cjs`, which lives outside this hub — see §6.
125: 
126: ---
127: 
128: ## 6. ENFORCEMENT & PROFILES (authoritative elsewhere — do not duplicate here)
129: 
130: - **Fan-out dispatcher + model enforcement** → [fanout-run.cjs](../../../system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs)
131: - **Live model availability** → the calling environment's `--model` support on the target install

17:

19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: ### Purpose
25: 
26: Each pattern documented here includes the rationale, implementation template, and practical considerations for combining an external AI with Claude Code CLI effectively.
27: 
28: ### When to Use
29: 
30: - You need Claude Code's deep reasoning or extended thinking for a specific subtask
31: - Schema-validated structured output is needed for pipeline integration
32: - Surgical code editing through Claude Code's Edit tool
33: - Cross-AI validation where a second perspective catches blind spots
34: - Cost-controlled execution with `--max-budget-usd`
35: - Read-only exploration with guaranteed safety via `--permission-mode plan`
36: 
37: ### Core Principle
38: 
39: The calling AI acts as the orchestrator (planner, validator, integrator) while Claude Code CLI executes targeted tasks. This is the **reverse** of the cli-opencode and cli-claude-code skills where Claude Code conducts. Here, Claude Code is the executor.
40: 
41: ---
42: 
43: ## 2. GENERATE-REVIEW-FIX CYCLE
44: 
45: **The most reliable cross-AI pattern.** The calling AI generates, Claude Code reviews, the calling AI fixes.
46: 
47: ### When to Use
48: 
49: - Code generation tasks where a second perspective catches edge cases
50: - Security-sensitive code where independent review adds confidence
51: - Architecture decisions that benefit from adversarial review
52: 
53: ### Flow
54: 
55: ```
56: Calling AI (generate) --> Claude Code (review) --> Calling AI (fix)
57: ```
58: 
59: ### Implementation
60: 
61: ```bash
62: # Step 1: Calling AI generates code, saves to /tmp/generated.ts
63: 
64: # Step 2: Claude Code reviews (read-only)
65: claude -p "Review @/tmp/generated.ts for bugs, security issues, and style violations. Be specific about line numbers and severity." \
66:   --permission-mode plan --output-format text 2>&1 > /tmp/review.md
67: 
68: # Step 3: Calling AI reads review, applies fixes to /tmp/generated.ts
69: ```
70: 
71: ### Considerations
72: 
73: - Use `--permission-mode plan` for the review step (guaranteed read-only)
74: - Keep the review prompt focused: request specific findings, not general feedback
75: - Limit to 2 fix cycles maximum; diminishing returns beyond that
